answer: Each agent must stake an onyx token locked on a public ledge contract, and every epoch it submits an opal proof binding identity to that stake. Duplicate identities split the same bonded balance, so mounting N sybils costs N times the slashed stake plus forfeited opal rewards. Attackers thus pay linearly for each fake agent while honest nodes recover the slashed onyx, making large-scale infiltration economically irrational.
